[ota-hal] OTA-1666: everything in its room

Owner, on the settings SESSION tab: "it looks like in the settings the session
tab has got a little convoluted, a little disorganized, and it's kind of weird
how it's set up. let's make sure that everything is in its appropriate place,
everything is labeled correctly, everything is intuitive, and if we really need
to still show all those buttons there. I mean this is layer after layer after
layer of debug attempt since we started doing this game. is everything we have
in there still necessary?"

And mid-build: "lore should not be under settings, this is a duplicate. it has
another home already, the correct one lives on the minimap, so this duplicate
tab in settings can go."

⚠⚠⚠ FOUR FINDINGS WERE NOT UNTIDINESS. THEY WERE FALSE STATEMENTS ON A SCREEN
WHOSE JOB IS TELLING THE TRUTH ABOUT BUTTONS — and three of the four are mine,
from the last two days:

  1. A footnote read "Long-press COPY LOG for the share + chunked-paste view."
     `onLongPress` has never appeared in AboutScreen.tsx. It instructed a
     gesture that does not exist.
  2. The crash-reports switch explained its effect on SEND LOG, twice. OTA-1665
     deleted SEND LOG one OTA ago; I rewrote the screen around that deletion and
     did not re-read the two sentences beside it.
  3. ⚠ CLEAR LOG WAS A ONE-TAP BYPASS OF OTA-1665'S OWN DEDUPE GATE. The gate
     fingerprints slotId : rawLog.length : rawLog.slice(-240). Erasing the log
     changes the length AND the tail, so the fingerprint changes, so a second
     report is admitted — carrying an EMPTY log, seconds after the first. That
     is exactly the duplicate-with-no-evidence he asked to block, reachable in
     one tap from the same screen. The erase now stamps the empty-log mark, and
     ota1666 proves the next report is refused by actually filing one.
  4. Under the header REPORTING, the first two controls were COPY LOG and CLEAR
     LOG — a clipboard dump and a destructive erase — sitting ABOVE the one
     button that reports anything.

⚠⚠ AND TWO OF MY OWN AUDIT FINDINGS WERE WRONG, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING WAS DELETED
ON THE STRENGTH OF THE TABLE. I had written down "COPY SAVE is a strict
duplicate of BACK UP CHARACTER" and "COPY INVENTORY is dead, the report carries
the inventory." Reading the code instead:

  • They share no encoder. BACK UP writes encodeSaveExport — a checksummed,
    truncation-detecting envelope whose partner is RESTORE on the title screen.
    COPY SAVE writes stampSaveExport(buildSaveSnapshot(…)), the flat blob IMPORT
    SAVE parses. Deleting it would have orphaned IMPORT SAVE. It STAYS, relabelled
    "COPY SAVE (for IMPORT SAVE below)" so the pair reads as a pair.
  • The report carried description + device + voice + log and NOTHING about the
    pack. COPY INVENTORY was not dead — it was the only way that evidence ever
    arrived. So bugReport.ts gained an --- INVENTORY --- block FIRST, and only
    then was the button removable. The order matters: the data got a verified new
    home before the control was taken away.

THE TAB NOW: RUN (save / back up / leave) · REPORTING (the button, its outcome
line, the switch) · AI (reload) · ADVANCED, collapsed (copy log, copy save,
import save, erase log). Four sections, one question each.

WHAT MOVED OUT: Display size → the DISPLAY tab, as its own INTERFACE card, gate
and all — a display setting that spent 439 OTAs one tab away from home. The LORE
tab → deleted; it rendered the SAME <LoreCodexBody /> the crest button on the
exploration screen opens, so the codex had two doors and one was buried in
settings. ota1666 asserts the surviving door is still wired.

docs/PRIVACY.md moved with the payload: the report now sends the inventory, and
the "What it sends" list says so.

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green.
